examples.ko: 동북부 지역에는 겨울에 눈이 많이 와요.
examples.en: It snows a lot in the northeastern region in winter.
My grandmother came from northeastern China.

examples.ko: 내일 태풍이 이 나라의 동북부를 지나갈 거예요.
examples.en: The typhoon will pass over the northeast of this country tomorrow.
This city is in the northeast of the country.
I want to take the train going to the northeast.
The news said the weather in the northeast will get worse.

explain: '동북쪽'은 방향이고 '동북부'는 그 방향에 있는 넓은 지역이에요. 날씨 예보나 뉴스에서 '서남부', '남동부'처럼 비슷한 말과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '동북쪽' is a direction, while '동북부' is the wide area lying in that direction. You hear it in weather forecasts and the news, alongside words like '서남부' and '남동부'.

en: out of the blue; random; abrupt

examples.en: Sorry for calling out of the blue.
What he said is so random.
A random question came up during the meeting.
This is out of nowhere, but are you free this evening?
Suddenly singing was a bit random.

examples.ko: 그는 뜬금없게도 시험 전날 이사를 했어요.
examples.en: Strangely out of the blue, he moved the day before the exam.

explain: '갑자기'는 일이 갑작스럽게 일어났다는 말이고, '뜬금없다'는 앞뒤 흐름과 맞지 않아서 이상하다는 느낌이 들어요. '뜬금없이', '뜬금없는'으로 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: '갑자기' just says something happened suddenly, but '뜬금없다' adds the feeling that it does not fit the situation at all. You mostly hear '뜬금없이' and '뜬금없는'.

examples.en: A mother's love is truly amazing.
That movie was made on the theme of maternal love.
I cried at the maternal love that tried to protect the child.
They say animals have maternal love too.

examples.ko: 그 드라마에서 모성애가 강한 엄마가 나와요.
examples.en: A mother with strong maternal love appears in that drama.

examples.ko: 모성애 때문에 엄마는 늘 자기보다 아이를 먼저 생각해요.
examples.en: Because of maternal love, a mother always thinks of her child before herself.

explain: 아빠 쪽 사랑은 '부성애'라서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 일상 대화에서는 '엄마의 사랑'이라고 하고, '모성애'는 영화, 뉴스, 글에서 더 자주 나와요. '모성애가 강하다/깊다', '모성애를 느끼다'로 써요.
explain_en: The paired word for a father's love is '부성애'. In everyday talk people say '엄마의 사랑', while '모성애' appears more in movies, news and writing. You say '모성애가 강하다/깊다' and '모성애를 느끼다'.

examples.ko: 회사에서 한 달 무급 휴가를 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a month of unpaid leave from the company.
Wouldn't an unpaid internship be tough?
This job is unpaid, so I'm hesitating.
He helped with the volunteer work without pay.
Making people work unpaid breaks the law.
My child was sick, so I took a few unpaid days off.

explain: '무급'의 반대말은 '유급'이에요. 보통 '무급 휴가', '무급 인턴'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 월급을 받는 휴가는 '유급 휴가'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite of '무급' is '유급', meaning paid. It usually sits in front of another noun, as in '무급 휴가' (unpaid leave) and '무급 인턴' (unpaid intern).

examples.ko: 칼이 너무 무뎌서 고기가 안 잘려요.
examples.en: The knife is so dull that it won't cut the meat.
The tip of the long-used pencil is blunt.
My hands lost feeling in the cold weather.
He tends to be slow at picking up on things.
Scissors with a dull blade are hard to use.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 무디면 친구가 서운해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you are too insensitive, your friends may feel hurt.

explain: '무디다'는 칼이나 연필처럼 날이나 끝이 날카롭지 않을 때도 쓰고, 사람의 감각이나 눈치가 둔할 때도 써요. 반대말은 '날카롭다'예요. '무뎌요', '무딘'으로 활용해요.
explain_en: '무디다' works for a dull blade or tip, and also for a person who is slow to sense things or read the mood. The opposite is '날카롭다'. It conjugates as '무뎌요' and '무딘'.

examples.en: I saw beautiful white porcelain at the museum.

examples.ko: 이 백자 항아리는 오백 년이 넘었어요.
examples.en: This white porcelain jar is over five hundred years old.
Many white porcelain pieces were made in the Joseon period.

examples.ko: 할머니 집에 작은 백자 접시가 있어요.
examples.en: There's a small white porcelain plate at my grandmother's house.
White porcelain looks neat because it is white.
I gave a white porcelain cup to my foreign friend.

explain: '백자'는 하얀 흙으로 구워 만든 도자기예요. 한국 도자기를 이야기할 때 푸른빛이 도는 '청자'와 함께 자주 나와요. 조선 시대 백자가 특히 유명해요.
explain_en: '백자' is pottery made from white clay. In talk about Korean ceramics it usually appears next to '청자', the blue-green kind. Joseon-era '백자' is especially famous.

examples.ko: 복어는 독이 있어서 아무나 요리하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Pufferfish is poisonous, so not just anyone may cook it.
At the aquarium, the pufferfish swelled up like a balloon.
My father likes pufferfish soup.

examples.ko: 복어를 잡으면 바로 바다에 놓아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: If you catch a pufferfish, you should put it back in the sea right away.
Pufferfish dishes are a bit expensive.

examples.ko: 저는 복어 사진을 찍으려고 아침 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I went early in the morning to take a photo of a pufferfish.

explain: '복어'는 독이 있어서 면허가 있는 요리사만 다룰 수 있어요. 한국에서는 맑은 국으로 먹는 '복어 지리'가 유명해요. 몸이 부풀어 오르는 모습으로 그림책에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '복어' is poisonous, so only licensed chefs can prepare it. In Korea it is best known as the clear soup '복어 지리'. Its habit of puffing up also makes it a common picture-book animal.

examples.en: The wind blows in from the northwest.
There's a mountain northwest of Seoul.
The ship moved slowly toward the northwest.

examples.ko: 이 지도에서 북서는 오른쪽 위가 아니라 왼쪽 위예요.
examples.en: On this map, northwest is the upper left, not the upper right.
Clouds are rolling in from the northwest.
My house is to the northwest of the school.

explain: '북서'는 방향 이름이라서 보통 '북서쪽', '북서풍'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 같은 방향을 '서북'이라고도 해서, '북동/동북', '남서/서남'처럼 순서를 바꿔 쓰는 말이 많아요.
explain_en: '북서' is a compass term and is usually followed by another word, as in '북서쪽' or '북서풍'. The same direction can also be called '서북', and many directions can be said in either order, such as '북동/동북' and '남서/서남'.

examples.en: The picture hanging on the wall is crooked.
He came out wearing his hat at a slant.
The chair is tilted, so it's uncomfortable to sit on.

examples.ko: 그는 요즘 모든 일을 삐딱한 눈으로 봐요.
examples.en: These days he looks at everything with a cynical eye.

examples.ko: 선생님 말에 삐딱하게 대답하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't answer the teacher in a rude, contrary way.
The book is stuck in at an angle.

explain: '삐딱하다'는 물건이 기울어진 모습에도 쓰고, 사람의 마음이나 태도가 곱지 않을 때도 써요. 비슷한 '비뚤다'는 모양이 곧지 않을 때 주로 써요. '삐딱하게'로 가장 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 내 말을 늘 삐딱하게 봐요.
phrases.en: to take something the wrong way
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 기운 것이 아니라 어떤 일을 좋지 않은 쪽으로 해석한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about a tilted gaze; it means reading something in a negative way.

explain_en: '삐딱하다' describes something tilted, and also a person with a sour or contrary attitude. The similar '비뚤다' is used mainly for shapes that are not straight. Most often you hear '삐딱하게'.

examples.en: The tiger is looking for prey.

examples.ko: 사냥꾼은 오늘 아무 사냥감도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: The hunter caught no game today.
Lions go after weak prey first.
In winter the prey becomes scarce, so animals have a hard time.

examples.ko: 그 새는 작은 곤충을 사냥감으로 삼아요.
examples.en: That bird takes small insects as its prey.

examples.ko: 잡은 사냥감을 마을 사람들과 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: They shared the game they caught with the villagers.

explain: '사냥감'은 사냥해서 잡는 동물이고, 먹잇감으로 쓰는 말은 '먹이'예요. 동물을 말할 때는 '먹이'를 더 많이 쓰고, 사냥하는 사람이 있을 때는 '사냥감'이 어울려요. 짝말은 '사냥꾼'이에요.
explain_en: '사냥감' is an animal that is hunted. For animals eating in general, '먹이' (food) is more common, while '사냥감' fits when a hunter is involved. Its partner word is '사냥꾼', the hunter.

examples.en: I rode a skateboard in the park on the weekend.
My younger brother got a skateboard as a birthday present.
Balancing on a skateboard is hard at first.

examples.ko: 저 아이는 스케이트보드를 아주 잘 타요.
examples.en: That kid is really good at skateboarding.

examples.ko: 스케이트보드를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when you ride a skateboard.

examples.ko: 길에서 스케이트보드를 타면 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Riding a skateboard on the street can be dangerous.

explain: '스케이트보드'는 바퀴가 달린 판 위에 서서 타는 놀이 기구예요. 손잡이가 달린 '킥보드'와 달라요. 눈 위에서 타는 '스노보드'와도 헷갈리지 마세요. '스케이트보드를 타다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '스케이트보드' is a wheeled board you stand on and ride. It differs from a '킥보드', which has a handle, and from a '스노보드', which is ridden on snow. You say '스케이트보드를 타다'.

examples.ko: 두 팀 감독이 경기 전부터 신경전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two team managers played mind games even before the match.
The department head and the section chief had a tense standoff in the meeting.

examples.ko: 가격을 두고 두 회사 사이에 신경전이 심해요.
examples.en: There's a heated war of nerves between the two companies over the price.

examples.ko: 형제가 리모컨을 두고 작은 신경전을 벌여요.
examples.en: The brothers have a little tussle over the remote control.
Before an election the candidates' sparring gets heated.
The mood was heavy because of the tension between them.

explain: '신경전'은 싸우지는 않지만 말이나 행동으로 서로 기싸움을 하는 상황에 써요. 보통 '신경전을 벌이다'로 말하고, 스포츠 뉴스나 회사 이야기에 자주 나와요. 몸이나 큰 소리로 맞붙는 다툼과 달리, 서로 눈치를 보며 긴장을 만드는 데 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: '신경전' is for a standoff where people do not fight openly but test each other with words and attitude. The usual pairing is '신경전을 벌이다', and it is common in sports news and workplace talk. Unlike a physical or shouting quarrel, the focus is on building tension while watching each other.

examples.en: The kids came running in, laughing boisterously.
I've never seen such an over-the-top greeting.
It's nothing serious, but you're making too much fuss.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말도 행동도 야단스러워서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: He stands out because both his words and his actions are showy.
Please congratulate her quietly, without a big fuss.
Grandmother greeted her grandchild with a big, fussy delight.

explain: '야단스럽다'는 소리나 행동이 지나치게 크고 요란해서 시끄러운 느낌이 들 때 써요. 비슷한 '호들갑스럽다'는 작은 일을 크게 떠드는 모습에 더 어울려요. 좋은 뜻으로 칭찬할 때는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '야단스럽다' is used when sound or behavior is too big and showy, so it feels noisy. The similar '호들갑스럽다' fits better when someone makes a big deal out of something small. It is rarely a compliment.

examples.en: The shepherd came down from the mountain driving his sheep.
Do you know the story of the boy who cried wolf?
When I was little, my dream was to be a shepherd.
A shepherd and a dog guard the sheep together.

examples.ko: 저 양치기는 하루 종일 풀밭에서 일해요.
examples.en: That shepherd works in the meadow all day.
The shepherd in the movie played a pipe.

explain: '양치기'는 양을 돌보는 사람이에요. 소를 돌보는 사람은 '소치기'라고 하지만 쓰임은 드물어요. '양치기 소년'은 거짓말하는 사람을 말할 때 비유로도 자주 써요. '양치질'과는 완전히 달라요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약속을 안 지켜서 양치기 소년이 됐어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓말을 자주 해서 진짜 말해도 믿어 주지 않는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It points to someone who lies so often that nobody believes them even when they tell the truth.

explain_en: '양치기' is a person who tends sheep. '양치기 소년' is also used as a metaphor for someone who lies. It is unrelated to '양치질', which means brushing your teeth.

examples.en: The restaurant owner greeted the customers.

examples.ko: 가게 업주는 요즘 손님이 줄어서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: The shop owner is worried because customers have decreased lately.
The business owners asked the government for help.

examples.ko: 이 미용실은 업주가 직접 머리를 잘라 줘요.
examples.en: At this hair salon the owner cuts the hair himself.
The owner and the staff cleaned together.
Rents went up, so business owners are having a hard time.

explain: '업주'는 식당, 가게, 숙박업소 같은 장사를 하는 주인을 부르는 말이라 뉴스나 서류에서 자주 나와요. 말로 직접 부를 때는 '사장님'이라고 해요. 직원은 '종업원'이에요.
explain_en: '업주' is the owner of a restaurant, shop, or lodging business, and is common in the news and on paperwork. When you speak to the person directly, you call them '사장님'. Their staff are '종업원'.

examples.ko: 실수를 해서 친구들 사이에서 웃음거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: I made a mistake and became a laughingstock among my friends.
I don't like becoming a laughingstock.
His strange clothes were a joke for a while.

examples.ko: 이 이야기는 두고두고 웃음거리로 남을 거예요.
examples.en: This story will remain something to laugh about for a long time.
I made a joke on purpose to ease the mood.
You must not make someone a laughingstock.

explain: '웃음거리'는 보통 '웃음거리가 되다', '웃음거리로 만들다'처럼 써요. 대부분 놀림의 뜻이 있어서 기분 나쁜 상황에 어울려요. 즐겁게 웃는 이야기는 '우스운 이야기'라고 해요.
explain_en: '웃음거리' is usually said as '웃음거리가 되다' or '웃음거리로 만들다'. It mostly carries a mocking tone, so it fits unpleasant situations. A pleasantly funny story is a '우스운 이야기'.

examples.en: At the museum I saw how primitive people lived.
Primitive people made tools out of stone and used them.

examples.ko: 아이가 원시인 옷을 입고 파티에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child went to the party in a caveman costume.
I read a story about primitive people discovering fire.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 없이 사니까 원시인이 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: Living without a smartphone makes me feel like a caveman.
They say primitive people lived in caves.

explain: '원시인'은 아주 오래전에 살던 사람을 말해요. 요즘 사람에게 쓰면 기술이나 문화에 어둡다고 놀리는 말이 될 수 있어서 조심해요. 가볍게는 '나는 원시인이야'처럼 장난으로 써요.
explain_en: '원시인' means people who lived in very ancient times. Used on a modern person it can mock them as out of touch with technology, so be careful. People jokingly say it about themselves, as in '나는 원시인이야'.

examples.en: On a cold day I think of mushroom hot pot.
I ate beef hot pot with my family.
When the hot pot boils, add more vegetables.
This restaurant's tripe hot pot is delicious.

examples.ko: 전골 국물에 라면 사리를 넣어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I added instant noodles to the hot pot broth and ate it.

examples.ko: 손님이 오면 전골을 테이블 위에서 끓여요.
examples.en: When guests come, we boil the hot pot on the table.

explain: '전골'은 재료를 담은 냄비를 상 위에서 직접 끓이면서 먹는 요리예요. '찌개'는 주방에서 끓여 내오는 경우가 많은 것과 달라요. 재료가 풍성해서 같이 먹는 사람이 많을 때 시켜요.
explain_en: '전골' is a dish boiled right at the table as you eat, in a pot already filled with ingredients. '찌개' is often brought out already cooked from the kitchen, which is different. It is full of ingredients, so people order it when eating with a group.

examples.ko: 호텔 지배인이 직접 방을 안내해 줬어요.
examples.en: The hotel manager showed us to the room himself.
If there's a problem, please call the manager.
The restaurant manager apologized to the customer.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 호텔에서 일해서 지배인이 됐어요.
examples.en: I worked at a hotel for ten years and became the manager.
The manager looks after the staff's schedules.

examples.ko: 예약이 안 되어 있어서 지배인과 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The reservation wasn't made, so I talked with the manager.

explain: '지배인'은 호텔, 식당, 극장 같은 곳에서 가게 일을 맡아 관리하는 사람이에요. 가게의 주인은 '사장'이나 '업주'이고, '지배인'은 주인 대신 일하는 사람이에요. 회사의 관리자는 '부장', '팀장'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: '지배인' runs the daily operation of a hotel, restaurant, or theater. The owner is the '사장' or '업주', while the '지배인' works on their behalf. Managers in a company are called '부장' or '팀장'.

examples.en: I ate sticky rice cake on the morning of the exam.
Sticky rice cake is chewy and tasty.
My friend gave me sticky rice cake as a gift for passing.
I miss the sticky rice cake my grandmother used to make.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 팥이 든 찰떡이 유명해요.
examples.en: This shop is famous for sticky rice cake filled with red beans.

examples.ko: 찰떡을 너무 급하게 먹으면 목이 막힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat sticky rice cake too fast, you can choke.

explain: '찰떡'은 찹쌀로 만든 찰진 떡이에요. 시험 전에 합격을 비는 선물로 '찰떡'이나 '찹쌀떡'을 주고받아요. 떡이 달라붙는 것처럼 붙으라는 뜻을 담았어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 떡이 잘 붙는 것처럼 두 사람이나 두 가지가 아주 잘 맞는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like sticky cake clinging together, two people or things fit each other perfectly.

explain_en: '찰떡' is a sticky cake made from glutinous rice. Before exams people give '찰떡' or '찹쌀떡' as a wish to pass, since it sticks like the hoped-for result.

en: stay up all night; work through the night

examples.en: I pulled an all-nighter last night because of the deadline.
The whole team worked through the night and finished the job.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 철야하면 다음 날 피곤해요.
examples.en: If you stay up all night before an exam, you're tired the next day.
I'll be working through the night again today.
We prepared a late meal for the staff working through the night.

examples.ko: 몸이 안 좋아서 철야하지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: I'm not feeling well, so I decided not to stay up all night.

explain: '철야하다'는 잠을 안 자고 밤을 새우며 일하거나 공부한다는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '밤을 새우다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 회사 일이나 기사에서는 '철야'를 써요. '철야 근무'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: '철야하다' means to go without sleep and work or study through the night. In daily talk '밤을 새우다' is more common, while '철야' appears in workplace and news contexts, often as a noun as in '철야 근무'.

examples.en: I took a sleeping bag when I went camping.
It was warm once I got inside the sleeping bag.
A winter sleeping bag is thicker than a summer one.
I borrowed a sleeping bag from my friend.
The children rolled out sleeping bags in the living room and slept.

examples.ko: 침낭은 접어서 작은 가방에 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sleeping bag can be folded into a small bag.

explain: '침낭'은 캠핑이나 등산에서 바닥에 펴고 그 안에 들어가 자는 주머니 모양의 잠자리예요. '침낭을 펴다/말다', '침낭에 들어가다'로 써요. 이불은 덮는 것이고 침낭은 몸 전체를 감싸요.
explain_en: '침낭' is a pouch-shaped sleeping bag you lay on the ground and climb into, used for camping and hiking. You say '침낭을 펴다/말다' and '침낭에 들어가다'. A blanket is something you cover with, while a sleeping bag wraps your whole body.

examples.en: I heard a hyena making a laughing sound at the zoo.
Hyenas hunt in packs.

examples.ko: 아프리카에서 하이에나와 사자가 싸우는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of a hyena and a lion fighting in Africa.

examples.ko: 하이에나는 다른 동물이 남긴 먹이도 먹어요.
examples.en: Hyenas also eat food that other animals leave behind.

examples.ko: 아이가 하이에나 그림을 그려서 벽에 붙였어요.
examples.en: The child drew a hyena and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 만화에 나오는 하이에나는 늘 나쁜 역이에요.
examples.en: The hyena in cartoons is always the bad guy.

explain: '하이에나'는 아프리카에 사는 동물이에요. 한국어에서는 남이 애써 얻은 것을 노리는 사람을 '하이에나 같다'고 부정적으로 비유해서 말하기도 해요. 동물원이나 다큐멘터리에서 무리 지어 사냥하고 우는 소리가 사람 웃음 같다고 자주 소개돼요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 성과만 노리는 하이에나 같아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 자체가 아니라, 남의 것을 노리고 빼앗으려는 사람을 부정적으로 비유하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about the animal; it negatively describes someone who preys on others' gains.

explain_en: '하이에나' is an animal of Africa. In Korean, someone who goes after what others worked hard for can be negatively called '하이에나 같다'. In zoos and documentaries it is often introduced as hunting in packs and making a sound like laughter.

examples.en: The child's smile is truly bright and innocent.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 늘 해맑은 얼굴로 인사해요.
examples.en: That child always greets people with a bright, innocent face.

examples.ko: 해맑게 웃는 모습을 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing her laugh so brightly makes me feel good.
Puppies are so carefree that just seeing them makes me happy.

examples.ko: 어른이 되어도 해맑은 마음을 잃고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: Even as an adult, I don't want to lose my innocent heart.

examples.ko: 그는 해맑았던 어린 시절을 가끔 떠올려요.
examples.en: He sometimes remembers his innocent childhood.

explain: '해맑다'는 얼굴이나 웃음이 맑고 순수해서 걱정이 없어 보일 때 써요. 아이나 강아지처럼 순수한 대상에 주로 쓰고, 어른에게 쓰면 철이 없다는 뜻으로 들릴 때도 있어요. '해맑게 웃다'로 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: '해맑다' describes a face or smile that is clear and pure, looking free of worries. It is used mostly for children and puppies, and for an adult it can sometimes sound like naive. The usual phrase is '해맑게 웃다'.

examples.en: You shouldn't badmouth a friend behind their back.
I heard my coworkers badmouthing the department head.
I feel uncomfortable around people who speak ill of others.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 모임에서 늘 다른 사람을 험담해요.
examples.en: That person always speaks ill of others at gatherings.
I feel bad about the gossip I spread yesterday.
Don't badmouth them; try talking to them directly.

explain: '험담하다'는 그 사람이 없는 곳에서 흉을 보는 거예요. 비슷한 '뒷담화하다'는 구어에서 더 편하게 쓰고, '비판하다'는 이유를 대서 잘못을 말하는 거라 달라요. 보통 '험담을 하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: '험담하다' is speaking ill of someone when they are not there. The similar '뒷담화하다' is the casual spoken version, while '비판하다' means criticizing with reasons, which is different. '험담을 하다' also works.

examples.en: He said what he thought without hesitation.
The player won with fearless play.
That child speaks without holding back.
Everyone was surprised by the blunt question.

examples.ko: 작년부터 이 회사는 거침없이 성장하고 있어요.
examples.en: Since last year this company has been growing without pause.

examples.ko: 거침없었던 그의 도전이 사람들에게 용기를 줬어요.
examples.en: His fearless challenge gave people courage.

explain: '거침없다'는 막힘이나 망설임 없이 쭉 나아가는 모습에 써요. 긍정적으로는 자신감과 속도를, 부정적으로는 눈치 없이 말하는 모습을 가리킬 수 있어요. 주로 '거침없이', '거침없는'으로 말해요.
explain_en: '거침없다' describes moving ahead without any block or hesitation. It can praise confidence and speed, or it can point to someone who speaks bluntly without reading the mood. You mostly hear '거침없이' and '거침없는'.

examples.en: In the morning I eat yogurt with raisins in it.
Raisin bread is the tastiest.
I don't like the raisins in cookies.
Raisins are made by drying grapes.

examples.ko: 아이가 간식으로 건포도를 한 줌 먹었어요.
examples.en: The child ate a handful of raisins as a snack.
I put raisins and nuts in the cake.

explain: '건포도'는 '마를 건(乾)'과 '포도'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 같은 '건'이 들어간 말로 '건어물'이 있어요. 한국 사람은 빵, 시리얼, 샐러드에 넣어 먹는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: '건포도' combines '건' (dried) and '포도' (grape). The same '건' appears in '건어물' (dried seafood). Koreans often have it in bread, cereal, and salads.

examples.en: Milk is a good source of calcium.
Sunlight is a source of vitamin D.

examples.ko: 이 공장이 도시에 전기를 보내는 공급원이에요.
examples.en: This plant is the source supplying electricity to the city.
Fish is good as a protein source.
The food supply was cut off, so people had a hard time.

examples.ko: 저는 새로운 단백질 공급원을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a new source of protein.

explain: '공급원'은 필요한 것을 내주는 곳이나 물건이에요. 영양이나 에너지 이야기에서는 '단백질 공급원', '에너지 공급원'처럼 자주 써요. 물건을 파는 사람이나 회사는 '공급자'나 '거래처'라고 해요.
explain_en: '공급원' is a place or thing that provides what is needed. In nutrition and energy talk it is used as '단백질 공급원' or '에너지 공급원'. A person or company that sells goods is a '공급자' or '거래처'.

en: return to farming; move to the countryside to farm

examples.en: My father retired and returned to his hometown to farm.

examples.ko: 도시에서 일하다가 귀농하는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are leaving city jobs to take up farming.
I'm thinking of going back to farming later.
I started apple farming after returning to the countryside.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 귀농한 지 삼 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three years since that couple moved to the countryside to farm.

examples.ko: 귀농하려면 먼저 땅과 집을 알아봐야 해요.
examples.en: To start farming in the country, you first need to look for land and a house.

explain: '귀농하다'는 도시에서 살다가 농사를 지으러 농촌으로 가는 거예요. 농촌으로 이사해서 농사를 하지 않고 사는 것은 '귀촌하다'라고 해서 달라요. 기사에서는 '귀농 귀촌'으로 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: '귀농하다' is leaving the city to farm in the countryside. Moving to the countryside without farming is '귀촌하다', which is different. In news the two are often written together as '귀농 귀촌'.

examples.en: I went to a billiard hall with friends and played a game.
A new billiard hall opened in my neighborhood.
How much is the billiard hall per hour?

examples.ko: 대학교 앞 당구장은 늘 학생들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: The billiard hall in front of the university is always crowded with students.
My father worked at a billiard hall when he was young.
It rained, so I spent time at the billiard hall.

explain: '당구장'은 당구를 칠 수 있는 가게예요. 한국에서는 '당구를 치다'라고 하고, '당구를 하다'도 써요. 같은 방식으로 '볼링장', '탁구장'이라고 하는 곳이 있어요.
explain_en: '당구장' is a shop where you can play billiards. The verb is '치다' as in '당구를 치다', and '당구를 하다' also works. The same '-장' pattern gives '볼링장' and '탁구장'.

examples.en: A new challenger takes on the champion.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 도전자가 백 명이나 나왔어요.
examples.en: A hundred challengers entered this competition.
The challenger kept running to the end without giving up.
He is the youngest challenger in this program.
I always work with a challenger's spirit.
Please give the challenger a round of applause.

explain: '도전자'는 대회에서는 챔피언에게 도전하는 사람을 말해요. 일상에서는 새로운 일에 용기를 내서 나서는 사람에게도 써요. 이미 이긴 사람, 곧 우승한 사람은 '챔피언'이나 '우승자'라고 해요.
explain_en: In a contest '도전자' is the person taking on the champion. In daily life it also fits someone bravely trying something new. The one who already won is the '챔피언' or '우승자'.

examples.en: I met a wild dog on the mountain path and was startled.

examples.ko: 들개는 무리를 지어 다니는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wild dogs often move around in packs.
An abandoned dog sometimes becomes a stray.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 들개 때문에 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: The villagers are very worried about the wild dogs.

examples.ko: 들개를 보면 가까이 가지 말고 피하세요.
examples.en: If you see a wild dog, avoid it and don't go near.

examples.ko: 다큐멘터리에서 아프리카 들개가 사냥하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw African wild dogs hunting in a documentary.

explain: '들개'는 주인 없이 들이나 산에서 사는 개예요. 버려져서 떠도는 개는 '유기견'이라고 해요. '들'은 야생의 뜻을 더해서 '들고양이', '들꽃'처럼 쓰여요.
explain_en: '들개' is a dog with no owner that lives in fields or mountains. A dog that was abandoned and wanders is called a '유기견'. The prefix '들' adds a wild feel, as in '들고양이' and '들꽃'.

examples.en: The bread that was just baked is nice and hot.
Drinking the piping hot broth relaxes my body.
In winter, hot hotteok is the best.
I like that the floor of the heated room is nice and warm.
This movie is a brand-new release.
Please eat while the rice is still piping hot.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 데일 만큼 뜨거울 때 쓰고, '따끈따끈하다'는 먹거나 만지기 좋은 정도로 따뜻해서 기분이 좋을 때 써요. 갓 나온 빵이나 국물에 자주 어울려요. 새로 나온 소식이나 작품에도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: '뜨겁다' is hot enough to burn, while '따끈따끈하다' is pleasantly hot, just right to eat or touch. It suits freshly baked bread or soup. It is also used figuratively for brand-new news or works.

examples.en: The children played on a raft on the river.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 나무로 뗏목을 만들어 강을 건넜어요.
examples.en: People long ago made rafts out of wood to cross rivers.
I went to Gangwon-do for a rafting experience.
A raft is drifting in from the sea.
In the movie the hero crosses the sea on a raft.
A raft is made by tying logs together.

explain: '뗏목'은 나무를 엮어 만든 것으로 사람이나 짐을 싣고 물 위를 가요. '배'와 달리 몸체가 따로 없고 통나무를 묶어서 만든 평평한 거예요. 공기를 넣은 고무 배는 '고무보트'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: '뗏목' is made of tied-together logs and carries people or goods on water. Unlike a '배', it has no hull; it is a flat platform of lashed logs. An inflatable rubber boat is called a '고무보트', which is a different thing.

examples.en: We did recreation activities at the company workshop.

examples.ko: 수학여행 때 레크리에이션 시간이 제일 재미있었어요.
examples.en: The recreation time was the most fun on the school trip.
The recreation instructor led the games.
I prepared recreation activities for the children.

examples.ko: 저녁 식사 후에 레크리에이션이 있을 거예요.
examples.en: There will be group games after dinner.
Thanks to the group games, we became much closer.

explain: 한국에서 '레크리에이션'은 보통 여럿이 모여 하는 게임이나 놀이를 말해서 '레크'라고 줄여 부르기도 해요. 혼자 즐기는 취미는 '취미'나 '여가 활동'이라고 해요. 단체 행사에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: In Korea '레크리에이션' usually means games and play done by a group, and is sometimes shortened to '레크'. Solo hobbies are called '취미' or '여가 활동'. You hear it often at group events.

examples.en: I went to the township office to get a document.
The township office helps villagers with their affairs.
A township office worker explained kindly.
Grandmother applied for her pension at the township office.

examples.ko: 우리 마을 면사무소는 오후 여섯 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The township office in our village closes at six in the evening.

examples.ko: 이사를 하면 면사무소에서 주소를 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: After moving, you have to change your address at the township office.

explain: '면사무소'는 시골의 '면'이라는 지역 단위 행정 기관이에요. 도시에서는 같은 일을 '주민센터'에서 해요. 면보다 큰 '읍'에는 '읍사무소'가 있어요.
explain_en: '면사무소' is the local government office of a '면', a rural area unit. In cities the same work is done at a '주민센터'. A '읍', which is larger than a '면', has an '읍사무소'.

examples.en: The wind is blowing and the door is rattling.
I replaced the old door with a new one.
The car door got dented, so I took it in for repair.
The door came off, so I have to put it back on.
The child cried after getting a hand caught in the door.
The wardrobe door won't open.

explain: '문'은 열고 닫는 장치 전체를 말하고, '문짝'은 그 문의 판자 부분만 가리켜요. 그래서 '문짝이 떨어지다', '자동차 문짝'처럼 문이 부서지거나 고칠 때 자주 써요. 방 입구의 문을 말할 때는 '문'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '문' refers to the whole door setup, while '문짝' points to the panel itself. So it is common when a door breaks or is repaired, as in '문짝이 떨어지다' and '자동차 문짝'. For the door of a room, just say '문'.

examples.en: I boiled instant noodles on a burner at the campsite.
I need to put new gas in the burner.

examples.ko: 바람이 불어서 버너 불이 자꾸 꺼져요.
examples.en: The wind keeps blowing out the burner flame.
I took a small burner when I went hiking.

examples.ko: 버너를 쓸 때는 불 조심을 해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful with fire when using a burner.

examples.ko: 친구가 새 버너를 사서 같이 써 봤어요.
examples.en: My friend bought a new burner and we tried it together.

explain: '버너'는 밖에서 요리할 때 쓰는 휴대용 불판이에요. 집 부엌에서 쓰는 건 '가스레인지'나 '인덕션'이라고 해요. 캠핑 이야기에서 '버너'와 '코펠'을 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '버너' is a portable stove for cooking outdoors. The ones in a home kitchen are a '가스레인지' or '인덕션'. In camping talk it often comes together with '코펠', the cooking pot set.

en: round and round; with a smile

examples.en: The ride spins round and round.
The child is spinning round and round on the spot.
A bird is circling in the sky.
I spun too much and my head is spinning.
The laundry spins round and round inside the washing machine.

examples.ko: 길을 못 찾아서 같은 곳을 빙글빙글 돌았어요.
examples.en: I couldn't find the way and went around the same place in circles.

explain: '빙글빙글'은 둥글게 계속 도는 모양을 나타내요. '돌다'와 함께 쓰고, 어지러울 때는 '머리가 빙글빙글 돌아요'라고 해요. 또 '빙글빙글 웃다'처럼 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모양도 나타내요. 비슷한 '뱅글뱅글'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '빙글빙글' shows something turning in a continuous circle. It goes with '돌다', and for dizziness you say '머리가 빙글빙글 돌아요'. It also describes a soft, silent smile, as in '빙글빙글 웃다'. The similar '뱅글뱅글' feels smaller and lighter.

examples.en: I had the wedding ring made of pure gold.
Pure gold is soft, so it bends easily.
I gave a pure gold ring for the baby's first birthday.
This necklace is real pure gold, so it's expensive.
I went to the jewelry shop to sell pure gold.
Grandmother passed down a pure gold bracelet to me.

explain: '순금'은 다른 금속이 섞이지 않은 금이에요. 한국에서는 아기 돌잔치나 결혼 때 '순금 반지'를 선물하는 문화가 있어요. 다른 금속이 섞인 금은 '합금'이나 '14K'처럼 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: '순금' is gold with no other metal mixed in. In Korea there is a custom of giving a '순금 반지' for a baby's first birthday or a wedding. Gold mixed with other metals is called '합금' or labeled like '14K'.

examples.en: Santa Claus rides a sleigh pulled by reindeer.
Reindeer live in cold northern regions.
I saw a reindeer in person in Finland.
A reindeer has large antlers on its head.
The child drew a reindeer on the Christmas card.

examples.ko: 눈 덮인 숲에서 순록 떼가 걸어가고 있어요.
examples.en: A herd of reindeer is walking through the snowy forest.

explain: '순록'은 추운 지방에 사는 사슴이에요. 한국 사람들은 크리스마스 이야기 때문에 '루돌프'라는 이름과 함께 떠올려요. 한국의 산에서 보는 '사슴'과는 다른 동물이에요.
explain_en: '순록' is a deer that lives in cold regions. Because of the Christmas story, Koreans associate it with the name '루돌프'. It is different from the '사슴' seen in Korean mountains.

en: before a meal; before a ceremony

examples.en: Please take this medicine before meals.
They say exercising before a meal is good for the body.

examples.ko: 식전에 물 한 잔을 마시는 습관이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of drinking a glass of water before meals.
The bread before the meal came out, so I ate it first.
You must wash your hands before eating.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 식전 삼십 분에 먹으라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said to take it thirty minutes before the meal.

explain: '식전'은 밥을 먹기 전이고 반대말은 '식후'예요. 약 봉투에 '식전 30분', '식후 30분'처럼 자주 적혀 있어요. 식당에서는 '식전 빵'처럼도 써요. 또 행사나 의식이 시작되기 전을 뜻해서 '식전 행사'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '식전' is before eating and its opposite is '식후'. You often see '식전 30분' or '식후 30분' on medicine packets, and in restaurants it appears as '식전 빵'. It can also mean before a ceremony begins, as in '식전 행사'.
